stories.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.summary: India will apply customs‑duty concessions on selected New Zealand imports from 20 October 2026. The concessions include zero basic duty on sheep meat, set duties on fish and wine, a 15 % duty on kiwi fruit, and unspecified rates for manuka honey. Dairy products remain excluded from the liberalisation.

stories.previousTitle: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.previousSummary: India will implement customs‑duty concessions for certain New Zealand imports from October 20, including zero basic duty on sheep meat, reduced rates on wine and fish, and preferential duties on manuka honey and kiwi fruit, with limited quantities permitted under tariff‑rate quotas. Dairy and other sensitive categories are excluded from the liberalisation.

stories.title: Trump’s 100% Russian oil tariff U-turn has a catch India can’t ignore
stories.summary: GTRI has warned that Donald Trump’s waiver of threatened 100% tariffs on Russian oil buyers offers India only temporary relief, as Washington can reinstate the duties at any time. The think tank cited US purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China and ongoing India-US trade talks as possible reasons for the move.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: Trump grants temporary waiver of 100% tariff on Russian oil for India
stories.previousSummary: President Donald Trump announced a waiver of the previously threatened 100 percent tariff on Russian oil for buyers, including India. The Global Trade and Investment (GTRI) think tank cautioned that the relief is temporary, noting that Washington could reinstate the duties at any time. GTRI pointed to U.S. purchases of Russian diesel, tariff protection for China and ongoing India‑U.S. trade talks as possible motivations, and advised New Delhi to protect its energy security and avoid permanent trade concessions.

stories.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
stories.summary: Donald Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

stories.previousTitle: Trump suspends Russia sanctions amid dispute with Zelensky
stories.previousSummary: Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night that suspended several sanctions against Russia that were scheduled to take effect two days later. The move prompted criticism from U.S. lawmakers and a sharp rebuke from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who said the United States was disregarding the sanctions. The suspension comes after a controversial U.S. deal to import Russian diesel and Ukraine’s claim that the administration is pulling back military support.
